first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, so a guarded simplification test is the most direct sustainable response. Limit it to simple self-serve/SMB workspaces, retaining the full flow for complex accounts because shortening onboarding previously increased churn there. Avoid promotional pricing despite competitor pressure because it lifted acquisition while materially reducing 30-day retention. Measure qualified activation, time-to-value, conversion, and 30-day retention.

final.rationale: Run a guarded onboarding simplification experiment for simple self-serve and SMB accounts, where prior evidence shows improved completion, activation, and time-to-value. Exclude complex-workspace accounts because the archived source confirms a 9% increase in 60-day churn when required setup steps are removed. Do not use promotional pricing: its 18% qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% decline in 30-day retention, which conflicts with sustainable long-term revenue. Evaluate completion, activation, time-to-value, qualified conversion, and 30-day retention.
